claim: Application Gateway for Containers' inference gateway states explicitly that routing directly to public or managed model provider endpoints is outside the scope of the GIE integration -- the inference gateway focuses on self-hosted inference workloads running on Kubernetes.
stance_target: GIE/InferencePool is designed to route to external or managed (non-self-hosted) model providers
scope_conditions: Microsoft Learn docs for Azure Application Gateway for Containers inference gateway (preview), last updated 2026-06-24
quoted_support: The inference gateway focuses on self-hosted inference workloads running on Kubernetes. Routing directly to public or managed model provider endpoints is outside the scope of this integration.

claim: An InferencePool includes a pod selector, target port information, and an endpoint picker reference; the EPP is responsible for selecting the endpoint for a request, and a single EPP is associated with a single pool.
stance_target: InferencePool's spec surface is defined entirely in terms of Pod selection (selector over Pods), reinforcing pods-only backend semantics
scope_conditions: Microsoft Learn docs, InferencePool compared with Service section
quoted_support: An InferencePool includes a pod selector, target port information, and an endpoint picker reference. The EPP is responsible for selecting the endpoint for a request. A single EPP is associated with a single pool.

claim: InferencePool endpoint picker references support two failure modes: FailOpen (gateway falls back to standard endpoint selection if the EPP is unavailable, preserving availability but possibly reducing routing quality) and FailClose (gateway rejects the request instead of routing without a required endpoint-selection decision).
stance_target: exact failure-mode semantics available on the EPP reference
scope_conditions: Microsoft Learn docs, Failure behavior section
quoted_support: FailOpen: If the EPP is unavailable or doesn't respond, the gateway can continue with standard endpoint selection for the pool... FailClose: If the EPP is unavailable or doesn't respond, the gateway rejects the request.

claim: Application Gateway for Containers runs a managed Body-Based Routing (BBR) processor that inspects an OpenAI-compatible request body, extracts the model name, and injects it as header X-Gateway-Model-Name so HTTPRoute can match on it for model-aware routing.
stance_target: mechanism by which model name is surfaced from request body to the Gateway API routing layer
scope_conditions: Microsoft Learn docs, Request flow / What the Gateway API Inference Extension provides sections
quoted_support: Body-based routing (BBR): A request processor that can inspect an OpenAI-compatible request body, extract the model name, and make it available to the gateway as the `X-Gateway-Model-Name` header for model-aware routing.

claim: In the current (v1) API surface described by this doc, InferenceModel has been replaced by InferenceObjective, a resource representing per-request serving priority via header x-gateway-inference-objective, used alongside InferencePool.
stance_target: current-generation resource name and mechanism for expressing request priority, superseding the older InferenceModel CRD
scope_conditions: Microsoft Learn docs, What the Gateway API Inference Extension provides / Example scenarios
quoted_support: InferenceObjective: A resource that represents request-serving objectives, such as priority, for requests that share an InferencePool... Use InferenceObjective resources and the x-gateway-inference-objective request header to assign serving priority.

claim: The EPP scores candidate endpoints via configurable plugins (e.g. queue depth, KV cache utilization, prefix-cache affinity); the available routing behaviors depend entirely on which scorer plugins the customer-provided EPP enables.
stance_target: the EPP's scoring/routing logic is explicitly plugin-based and thus customizable, including for non-standard backend signal sources
scope_conditions: Microsoft Learn docs, What the Gateway API Inference Extension provides section
quoted_support: The EPP receives request metadata, scores candidate model server pods by using configurable plugins (for example, queue depth, KV cache utilization, and prefix-cache affinity), and returns the selected endpoint. Because endpoint selection runs in the EPP, the available routing behaviors depend on the scorer plugins that your EPP enables.
